description:
Dispatcher for note creation, rendering, editing and deletion; with no subcommand it runs `new`.

Subcommands:
  new — create a new note and open it (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  copy [FILTER] — pick a note, copy contents to a new timestamp (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  strip [FILTER] — pick a note, copy and remove the body for use as a template (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  edit [FILTER] — pick a note, open in the default editor (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  nano [FILTER] — pick a note, open in nano (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  last — open the most recently-created note; the only non-interactive subcommand
  delete [FILTER] — pick a note and permanently delete it (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  cat [FILTER] — pick a note and print it to stdout (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  pdf [FILTER] — pick a note and render to PDF plus markdown (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  minutes [FILTER] — pick a note and render meeting minutes: TOC plus AGREED/RESOLVED/ACTION summary (INTERACTIVE, do not call)
  agenda [FILTER] — pick a note and render a meeting agenda (INTERACTIVE, do not call)

Args:
  SUBCOMMAND — one of the names above; omitted means `new`
  FILTER — optional case-insensitive substring filter for the picker

Examples:
  ["last"]

Notes:
  Every subcommand except `last` opens a picker and reads a selection from stdin. With no terminal it consumes EOF and behaves unpredictably rather than failing. Call only `last`.
  To find notes without a picker, use `search notes`. To read a note body, resolve its path via `search` and read the file directly.
  Body keywords recognised in note text: ACTION: (ingested by `tasks`), TASK: (machine-written, never hand-write), AGREED:, RESOLVED:, !: (callout).
  Rendering subcommands write into the export directory, by default the user's Downloads folder, and require pandoc plus a LaTeX engine.

BLOCKED: new, copy, strip, edit, nano, last, delete, cat, pdf, minutes, agenda. These subcommands are refused and calling one returns an error. Do not attempt them.
